title: Solar Orbiter Data Delivery Interface Control Document
organisation: European Space Agency, ESOC (OPS-GDS, Solar Orbiter Data Systems)
status_notes: Status 'Final', Issue 1 Revision 2, date of issue 26/06/2019 (PDF p. 1); digitally signed by P. Margarido on 2019-06-26 (PDF p. 2). Classified 'ESA UNCLASSIFIED – For Official Use'. Revision 2 is described as 'Tidy up and alignment with BepiColombo DDID' (PDF p. 3).
summary:
The Solar Orbiter Data Delivery Interface Control Document (DDID), SOL-ESC-IF-05011 issue 1 revision 2 (26 June 2019), prepared at ESOC by L. Michienzi and P. Margarido and approved by the Solar Orbiter operations, ground segment and science managers. It is the mission-specific complement to the generic EDDS External User ICD and describes how the Science Ground Segment (SGS) and Principal Investigators obtain Solar Orbiter data from the MOC's Data Dissemination System (DDS), which is based on the ESOC EGOS Data Dissemination System (EDDS).

The document covers the data exchange concept (HTTPS web interface, EDDS client, XML batch and stream requests, SFTP delivery, scheduled requests and file subscriptions), operational assumptions, quotas and access restrictions by APID, SPID, parameter, file and time range, server set-up (cold-redundant prime and backup), security, backup and availability (at least 95% over a month), and the mapping of each data type onto the MCS long-term archive (PARC for packets and reports, DARC for parameters, FARC for files).

Its most technical part, chapter 7, documents the SCOS-2000 packet (TDEV) format as delivered: the common header fields (filing and creation times, simulation flag, ground station IDs, packet type, structure version 5, time-stamp policy and time quality, stream IDs mapped to virtual channels, filing key = SPID, mission ID 650, MIB release and issue), the TM header (TPSD, RouteID data unit type and qualifier, APID, SSC, PUS type and subtype), the TC header (uplink, execution and last-update times, PTV flag) and the handling of missing frames. Chapter 8 lists the data products, including the MCS-internal packets on APID 1966 and the time-correlation packets, command history, auxiliary file types, and service-13 TM files with their metadata event packets. Chapter 10 specifies RAPID files, the nominal OGS-to-SGS packet transfer via GFTS, with their naming and record format.

key_points.text: The Solar Orbiter DDID is a mission-specific complement to the generic EDDS External User ICD [A-1]; the two are meant to be read together, and the DDID only gives Solar Orbiter specifics.

The primary distribution mechanism is the EDDS (HTTPS web interface, EDDS client, XML batch or stream requests, SFTP delivery); the nominal OGS-to-SGS distribution uses GFTS to forward RAPID binary files containing all packets processed and archived by the MCS.

DDS responses come from the MCS long-term archive: packets, events and TC data from PARC, auxiliary and TM files from FARC, and TM parameters from DARC; spacecraft TM is normally available within seconds of ground-station reception.
All DDS data are big-endian; times are 4 bytes of seconds since 1 January 1970 (not counting leap seconds) followed by 4 bytes of microseconds.

Each SCOS-2000 (TDEV) packet has a common header followed by a TM, TC or event specific header; for TM the packet data is the full un-stripped source packet starting with the CCSDS primary header version number.
The MCS stores an extra TC packet per command with SPID 200 holding the static MIB PTV/CEV details; external users should ignore it. TC packets use SPIDs 100 and 200.
Common header: packet type 1 TM, 2 TC, 3 Event; structure version 5 for Solar Orbiter; ground station IDs include 21 Kourou, 22 Perth, 23 New Norcia, 24 Cebreros, 25 Malargüe and 30 Maspalomas.

Time-stamp policy values are 0 creation time, 1 frame transmission time (ERT minus propagation delay) and 2 correlated SCET, with time quality 0 good, 1 inaccurate, 2 bad; stream IDs 1000-1003 map to online VC0-VC3 (real-time, playback, science, file transfer).

The filing key is the SCOS-2000 SPID that maps to the MIB packet definition; the mission ID is 650, and the DB Rel and DB Iss fields record the MIB VDF_RELEASE and VDF_ISSUE used when the packet was archived.
The TM header's RouteID low byte gives the data unit type (0 transfer frame, 1 source packet, 2 internal MCS packet) and a qualifier (for example 1 bad, 2 idle, 4 service 9 time packet).
The TC command details data are produced by overlaying a C++ class on memory of a 32-bit platform, so fields are 32-bit aligned with padding.

MCS-internal packets use APID 1966 (SPIDs 66810-66999) and should be filtered out, except the time-correlation packets: report SPID 66840 (TM 164,1), time couple 66841 (164,2) and coefficients 66842 (164,3). Spacecraft time packets have APID 0.
Service-13 TM files are stored in FARC as 'DLPP Files' named <PS_ID>_<file_reconstruction_timestamp>, with metadata in event packets of SPID 4000.

RAPID files are named PARC_<Type>_<FirstPacketTime>__<LastPacketTime>, close every 50 seconds, and contain length-prefixed records with an action type (0 insert, 1 update, 2 delete) and a sync marker 0x1ACFFC1D before each SCOS-2000 packet.

notes: The PDF has 35 pages; the extracted text has an empty 36th page. Printed page numbers are one lower than PDF page indices (PDF p. 7 is printed 'Page 6/35'), and the table of contents uses printed numbers. The change record prints the first issue as 'Issue 11, Revision 00' in the first table but 'Issue 1, Rev 0' in the second (PDF p. 3). Several cross-references in the text are broken: empty '[]' where a document ID should be, and 'Error! Reference source not found.' (PDF pp. 16, 19); a reference to 'section 0' for time correlation remains (PDF p. 27). The RAPID size is still 'approximately TBC MB' (PDF p. 33) although the change record says TBCs were removed. The section 7.1.3 heading lacks its number in the text layer (PDF p. 24). The file is the signed version ('_signed_PM'); footnote 2 says EDDS 2.3 schema definitions are attached to the PDF, but attachments were not extracted. The distribution list (PDF p. 4) and server host names/IP addresses (PDF pp. 11-14) are operational details not reproduced here.
